items.q: We pay for exchange DI. When does a package make sense?

items.q: When is polypropylene the wrong choice?

items.q: How do we size generation against storage?

items.q: Single-pass or double-pass RO?
items.a: Single-pass reverse osmosis (RO) with electrodeionization (EDI) suits feed with moderate dissolved solids. Double pass adds margin on conductivity, total organic carbon and silica for high-solids feed.

items.q: How do you handle cold winter feed?
items.a: Rated at 25 °C, reverse osmosis (RO) can lose a third or more of its output at 5 °C. We size at your coldest feed, or add a heat exchanger.

items.q: Our supply is chloraminated. What changes?
items.a: Chloramine damages reverse osmosis (RO) membranes, so it is removed first, which releases ammonia. Ammonia can pass RO when pH is raised for CO₂ control, so we design both together.

items.q: How is the PP skid sanitized?

items.q: How do you measure L/D?
items.a: L runs from the main pipe's inside wall to the valve seal point; D is the branch's inside diameter. We measure every tee and sample valve and list each in the dead leg register.

items.q: How do you keep flow turbulent when several outlets open?
items.a: We size pipe and pump for the worst-case outlet combination, not the average. At the site acceptance test (SAT), we open those outlets together and record return flow.

items.q: Is your system USP certified?

items.q: Which edition of each standard do you design to?
